newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan says will adjust policy on stock rally.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan says will adjust policy on stock rally.

text.p: Taiwan's central bank said on Tuesday it would adjust its monetary policy at an "appropriate time" following the stock market's recent surges to hit repeated seven-year highs.

"The central bank will adjust its monetary policy at an appropriate time," a central bank official quoted deputy central bank governor Hsu Chia-tung as saying late on Monday after the stock index closed at another seven-year high at 9,593.54 points.

"Based on good intention, I want to ask investors to 'think danger when reaching high.' (The central bank) will continue its 'do more, say little' and 'not-too-loose' monetary policy," Hsu was quoted as saying.

In March when the stock market rallied, Hsu made similar comments to cool the stock market. Several legislators later accused Hsu of trying to dampen the market, thus forcing central bank governor Sheu Yuan-dong to declare that the central bank would not comment on the stock market.
The central bank has recently reiterated that it would maintain its "stable-to-loose, but not-too-loose" monetary policy.
Analysts said the move was seen to boost the recovering domestic economy, but at the same time, the central bank also hoped liquidity would not be too high as to fuel a liquidity-driven stock rally.
